result.title: SteadyThought: Mitigating LLM Under-Thinking via Thought-Level Preference Optimization
result.summary: Flexible switching between reasoning trajectories (i.e., thought switching) has significantly enhanced the reasoning capabilities of Large Reasoning Models (LRMs). However, existing models often switch excessively yet fail to sustain promising reasoning thoughts, a phenomenon termed "under-thinking". While recent efforts suppress switching to mitigate this, such over-correction may discard valuable trajectories. To address this challenge, we propose Steady Thought (ST), a novel thought-level preference optimization framework. ST formalizes under-thinking as a preference issue at switching points, forcing single-path continuations from identified points to yield high-quality reasoning. Then, ST performs thought-level preference optimization by treating the newly generated response as preferred and the original one as dis-preferred. Experiments across multiple models and datasets show that ST effectively reduces token consumption, achieving reductions of up to 63.8%, while maintaining strong reasoning accuracy. Further analysis suggests that ST helps models acquire a generalizable ability to reduce redundant switching across domains and languages. Code is available at https://github.com/MIRALab-USTC/SteadyThought.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文针对大推理模型「思考不足」（频繁切换却无法维持有前景的推理轨迹）提出 SteadyThought 框架，在切换点构造单路径续写，并以「新续写为偏好、原回复为非偏好」做思维级偏好优化，在多模型与数据集上最多减少 63.8% token 消耗且保持准确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本工作，但其「在决策点比较不同续写路径并做偏好优化以抑制冗余切换」的训练思路，可能可供核查如何训练 VLM 维持 latent 推理状态、控制切换与停止决策。
